item.title: Saudi Arabia says preparations on for 2027 AFC Asian cup
item.description:
Saudi Arabia says preparations on for 2027 AFC Asian cup

Saudi Arabia has said preparations for the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, due to begin on 7 January in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar, remain on schedule despite escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom.

The tournament's local organising committee said that work was continuing in coordination with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), amid concerns over escalation in fighting that has led to postponement of several sporting events.

AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa said on Wednesday that a final decision could wait until the end of November and "we could move back a year to 2028 if we need to".

item.title: Future of western security is at stake in Yemen civil war, says country’s former PM
item.description:
Maeen Abdulmalik Saeed says Iran-backed militia’s use of drones represents ‘new era of radical terrorism’

The future of western security is being fought out in the mountains and hills surrounding the south-western Yemeni city of Taiz, the country’s former prime minster has said.

Maeen Abdulmalik Saeed, now an adviser to Yemen’s president, said it would be catastrophic if the city fell to the Iran-backed Houthi rebels, since control of the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait in the Red Sea and the road to Aden – the site of the UN-recognised government – would be lost.

item.title: Iraq appoints leader from Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq as deputy PM
item.description:
Iraq appoints leader from Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq as deputy PM

Iraq’s parliament has approved Laith al-Khazali, a senior figure from the Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq movement, as a deputy prime minister.

The United States designated the group a "foreign terrorist organisation" in 2020.

Khazali is the brother of the movement’s leader, Qais al-Khazali. Washington designated both brothers as "specially designated global terrorists", citing attacks including a 2007 assault that killed five US soldiers. The US Treasury also sanctioned them in 2019 over the killing of protesters in Iraq.

Lawmakers on Thursday approved three deputy prime ministers and 11 ministers, completing Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The appointments include Nayef al-Shammari as defence minister and Yasir al-Maliki as interior minister.

Zaidi's government has pledged economic reforms, anti-corruption measures and efforts to strengthen state institutions — but faces steep challenges, including rebuilding an economy battered by regional instability, tackling endemic corruption, and reining in Iran-allied armed groups, according to Reuters.

item.title: Houthis claim Saudi reconnaissance drone downed over Marib
item.description:
Houthis claim Saudi reconnaissance drone downed over Marib

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree has said the group shot down a Saudi Wing Loong II armed reconnaissance drone over Marib governorate.

In a statement posted on Telegram, Saree said the drone had been carrying out “hostile activities” in the governorate’s airspace.

Earlier, Houthis claimed responsibility for the attack on the government headquarters in Aden, with Saree describing the building as housing "Saudi war operations room".

item.title: Saudi-led coalition destroys drone headed towards Eastern Province, spokesman says
item.description:
Saudi-led coalition destroys drone headed towards Eastern Province, spokesman says

A drone launched towards Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province was intercepted and destroyed, Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Major General Turki al-Maliki said, without specifying the source of the drone and whether it caused any damage, according to Al Jazeera.

Earlier, Houthis claimed the deadly attack on the Saudi-backed Yemeni government's headquarters in Aden.

The US government could spend hundreds of thousands of dollars on a media campaign in South Africa to figure out why more white Afrikaners are not applying to become refugees to the US, as Donald Trump had hoped.

State department officials, according to an August proposal seen by the Guardian, outlined a roughly $335,000 research and advertising effort after applications to the refugee program “trended lower than expected” since Afrikaners were allowed to apply directly online in November 2025. The document, written by the US mission in South Africa with a department research unit for the embassy in Pretoria, admits officials know little about why.

item.title: Houthi missiles strike Yemen presidential palace, killing five
item.description:
Attack was the first on Aden’s Al-Maashiq palace ⁠in the latest fighting between ​the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia

Yemen’s Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing five people, the government said, as the Saudi-led coalition listed dozens of Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure in ⁠recent weeks.

The attack was the first on Aden’s Al-Maashiq palace ⁠in the current conflict between ​the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia. The palace is the seat of Yemen’s Saudi-backed and internationally recognised government.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes as Trump ‘energy ceasefire’ collapses
item.description:
Moscow sends swarms of drones to attack infrastructure in central Ukraine as Zelenskyy says Kyiv will restart strikes on Russian oil refineries

The White House’s unilateral effort to negotiate an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine has collapsed as Moscow sent a record swarm of drones overnight to attack infrastructure in central Ukraine and Kyiv appeared to resume strikes on Russian oil refineries despite warnings from Donald Trump.

Moscow accused Ukraine of launching a strike against a Russian oil refinery in the Ryazan region, its first since Trump abruptly declared an “energy ceasefire” that neither Russia nor Ukraine said they had agreed to.
